text:
Maya: Pushed a new figma for the multi-canary legend + compact stack. Wanted quick 🙏 on VoiceOver order and small-screen wraps — https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ/multi-canary-legend (frame: Legend / compact)
Priya: Scanned quickly — order looks visually fine but VoiceOver reads 'Canary B, 20%' before the 'status' pill (running/paused). Might confuse keyboard users. Can you swap semantic order so status is first in DOM? @Maya
Maya: good catch. The visual order needs to stay the same though. Thinking aria-label on the status pill and `aria-hidden` on the decorative percentage? Thoughts?
Sam: We need to keep the quick rollback affordance prominent. If we change DOM order, ensure focus still lands on the variant row not the legend control. Low risk but flagging for QA.
Jordan: For React: swapping DOM order is easy, but we should avoid layout shift. I can add `order` CSS and keep semantic structure correct. Priya, aria-label approach might be simpler.
Priya: aria-label can work but avoid relying on it for meaning. Better pattern: keep status early in DOM, visually re-order with CSS `flex-direction: row-reverse` so assistive tech sees status first and sighted users see the same visual. Also add `aria-describedby` on the row linking to the status element.
Luca: Prototype CSS idea:

```
.variant-row { display:flex; align-items:center; }
.legend { order: 2; }
.status { order: 1; }
```

Will add `aria-describedby="status-for-<id>"` with a short label.
Maya: Nice. Two other nits: 1) on very narrow widths the legend chips wrap and push the rollback CTA down — looks crowded. 2) color contrast on the 'paused' pill is 3.8:1 on the darker theme.
Jordan: For (1) we can collapse into a single overflow chip with "+2" and hover/tooltip to expand. That keeps the row compact. For (2) I'll tweak tokens — or use an outlined pill in dark mode.
Sam: I prefer overflow chip to avoid vertical growth. But ensure keyboard access to expand the overflow and reveal variants.
Priya: Keyboard+screenreader: overflow must be a button with `aria-expanded` and a visible focus ring. When expanded, the list should be a `role="listbox"` or `menu` depending on interactions.
Maya: Agree. Also wording: current copy "Roll back variant" reads a little heavy — can we test "Revert" vs "Roll back" in microcopy? @Sam
Sam: Let's A/B test the CTA copy in the next canary: variant A = "Roll back" (current), variant B = "Revert" with confirmation wording changed to "Are you sure you want to revert to {version}?" Keep analytics event `deploy.rollback.click` with `label: copy_variant`.
Luca: I'll add analytics flag and a feature flag combo: `canary_legend_v2` for safe rollout.
deploy-bot: posted a link to the staging build: https://staging.redwood.ai/deploys/legend-v2
Maya: Thanks — I'll update figma with the DOM notes and a narrow-width frame. Priya, can you review once I push the a11y annotations?
Priya: Yup, will check after the updates. Quick checklist for implementation:
- status element early in DOM (but visually unchanged)
- overflow chip as keyboard button + `aria-expanded`
- focus trap not needed — keep it a simple popover
- contrast token >= 4.5:1 for critical pills

Maya: Perfect. Landing plan: Jordan implements DOM/CSS tweaks this sprint, Luca hooks analytics and overflow interaction, Sam will wire the A/B test. QA pass for canary next week. :thumbsup:
